title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: A professor in sustainable built environment and building science combines advanced research with teaching, doctoral supervision, funded projects and leadership in sustainable architecture and construction.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes the Ph.D. is completed or is the student's current doctoral stage. If the student is still pursuing the Ph.D., the 2026–2030 section should be read as the transition from doctoral researcher to postdoctoral/assistant-professor-level researcher.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Convert Ph.D. research into publications, teaching experience, research projects and an academic appointment.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Establish a recognisable research niche in building performance, climate-responsive design, materials, energy, or sustainable construction.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead funded research, doctoral supervision, interdisciplinary teams and institutional sustainability initiatives.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Become a senior academic authority through research leadership, policy contribution, mentoring and international collaboration.

blocks.text: Note on the 4-year honours variant

The BCA-specific 4-year honours structure does not apply to this Ph.D. route. The relevant progression is Ph.D. → postdoctoral/academic appointment → Assistant Professor → Associate Professor → Professor, subject to the institution's recruitment and promotion rules.

rows.text: Thermal comfort · energy modelling · daylight · simulation
Indoor air quality · comfort · human performance

blocks.text: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046

Move from being a specialist researcher to a research-group leader. Build doctoral supervision capacity, win larger interdisciplinary grants, work with government and industry, publish synthesis research, and connect building science with climate adaptation, energy transition, digital simulation and resilient urban development.
At Ph.D. level, conventional internships are less useful than research fellowships, visiting positions, project appointments and industry research collaborations.

items.text: ANRF National Post Doctoral Fellowship — eligibility gate: Ph.D./eligible equivalent in specified science, engineering and medical areas plus scheme-specific age conditions. Confirm whether the proposed building-science research falls within the current disciplinary scope.
Institutional postdoctoral fellowships — eligibility gate: Ph.D. plus the host institution's discipline, age and publication requirements.
Research-project positions — eligibility gate: project-specific technical qualifications and selection.
ICSSR schemes — relevant only where the research is genuinely within eligible social-science disciplines; check the official site applicability to an architecture/building-science project.

Career progression
Ph.D. Researcher → Postdoctoral Researcher / Assistant Professor → Associate Professor → Professor → Research Chair / Centre Director → Distinguished or Senior Professor → Emeritus Professor
Typical years vary considerably by institution, publication record, vacancies and promotion rules.
PhD / advanced research routes

A senior professor in this field should increasingly shape the research agenda rather than only execute individual projects. The strongest profile combines a substantial publication record, doctoral graduates, competitive grants, industry and government partnerships, international collaboration and measurable impact on sustainable buildings. Emeritus or senior-scholar work can then focus on mentoring, major research syntheses, policy advice and long-term academic stewardship.
